ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The signal flow graph in the attached figure has one main forward path from left to right: R(s) -> X1 -> X2 -> X3 -> X4 -> X5 -> C(s). The forward branch gains are sequentially 1, G1, G2, 1, G3, G4, so the total gain of the unique forward path is P = G1 G2 G3 G4. There are three feedback loops in the figure: the lower left loop is labeled -H1, combined with forward gains G1 and G2, the loop gain L1 = -G1 G2 H1; the lower right loop is labeled -H2, combined with forward gains G3 and G4, the loop gain L2 = -G3 G4 H2; the upper large loop is labeled -H3, combined with forward gains G2 and G3, the middle X3->X4 branch gain is 1, therefore the loop gain L3 = -G2 G3 H3. Reasoning: The only pair of non-touching loops is L1 and L2, and their product is L1 L2 = G1 G2 G3 G4 H1 H2. All loops touch the unique forward path, so the cofactor of this forward path Delta_1 = 1. By Mason's gain formula, Delta = 1 - (L1 + L2 + L3) + L1 L2 = 1 + G1 G2 H1 + G3 G4 H2 + G2 G3 H3 + G1 G2 G3 G4 H1 H2. Therefore C(s)/R(s) = P Delta_1 / Delta.
